lens: validity, reliability, fairness, and evaluation design

findings.observation: The four cases now predeclare terminal status and tool order, but all four share the same no_action and three-tool expectation; none defines whether decision-relevant inputs were understood, which evidence must support the outcome, or what safe semantic behavior distinguishes refusal, clarification, and true no-action.
findings.evidence: eval-agent-lab.tsx defines four visible cases with identical expectedTerminal and expectedTools; traces 0be9a8d243bfbf67a0e78e8afc68dfcd, 96e7e0e1e7fe48d2026cfc0901ea61ba, 7983a7fc3bf63c3a2ff9542130b0b54c, and dcffc15fa137ee86e3a67f3d63cba437 all pass those mechanics while semantic_outcome_quality remains needs_review.
findings.user_impact: The suite can catch control-plane regressions but cannot reject a confidently wrong interpretation or prove that prompt injection, ambiguity, and ranking requests were handled for the right semantic reason.
findings.recommendation: Version atomic case expectations for required capabilities, terminal reason, required and forbidden tools, evidence citations, abstention or clarification behavior, prohibited claims, and exact external-effect boundary.
findings.verification: Seed wrong refusal, ambiguity, evidence, ranking, and capability-coverage outputs; each fails its own assertion while a correct case passes without a composite candidate score.

findings.observation: The set is four visible English prompts with no held-out cases, paraphrase or language slices, repeated stochastic runs, paired baseline, human gold adjudication, or critical false-pass budget.
findings.evidence: 01-start.jpg exposes all four authored scenarios; the trace index stores independent runs but no suite grouping, baseline, repeat stability, or per-slice counts.
findings.user_impact: A prompt or model change can appear improved through familiarity or random variation while regressing identity, evidence, language, or rare-harm cases.
findings.recommendation: Create versioned dev and held-out synthetic suites, run candidate-versus-baseline pairs, and report exact per-case counts, repeat stability, abstention coverage, and critical false passes before aggregate convenience metrics.
findings.verification: An untouched suite produces reproducible per-case diffs and blocks release on any unsupported external action, identity merge, candidate ranking, or evidence-free confirmed state.

strengths: The current version predeclares and deterministically checks terminal status and ordered tools.
Mechanical assertions remain atomic and inspectable rather than collapsing into one Agent score.
The ranking case targets a prohibited candidate-worth and acceptance-probability construct, and the platform does not rank a person.
missing_evidence: No machine-checkable semantic evidence or capability-coverage schema.
No independently authored held-out suite, human gold set, or grader calibration.
No live multimodal model, repeated stochastic run, language slice, or paired baseline.
open_questions: Which semantic failures are absolute gates even when aggregate suite performance improves?
